subject.title: [Bug] Agent context window fragmentation during concurrent subagent tool calls

question: Should concurrent native subagent completions remain push-based in completion order, or should OpenClaw deliberately buffer them into spawn order?
rationale: The issue does not show broken correlation under the current identifier-bearing event contract, while the proposed fix changes latency and orchestration semantics.

options.title: Preserve Push Order
options.body: Require a current-main transcript proving wrong result-to-task association, then fix the narrow correlation defect without buffering unrelated completions.

options.title: Adopt Spawn Order
options.body: Define deterministic spawn-order delivery as the product contract and accept that faster children may wait for slower earlier calls.

recommendation.title: Preserve Push Order
recommendation.body: Require a current-main transcript proving wrong result-to-task association, then fix the narrow correlation defect without buffering unrelated completions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work connects this contributor most directly to Codex app-server protocol and native subagent lifecycle behavior.
